Because core methods/results are unavailable, the study cannot be confirmed to meet all inclusion criteria; excluded and fulltext_incomplete=true.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (visual object and spatial delayed-recognition), which falls within executive function domains (I9). It reports within-participant contrasts comparing memory-delay conditions with active secondary-task conditions (e.g., Delay_location/no-distraction vs Delay_location/saccades; Delay_object/no-distraction vs Delay_object/passive listening), satisfying I6. The study used task-based fMRI (I5) and provides group-level whole-brain, voxelwise analyses with spatially normalized maps and tables of coordinates (I7,I8). Participant demographics and health status, imaging modality, and task paradigms are reported (healthy adults, ages ~22; I10). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, include active control conditions, are empirical human neuroimaging with healthy adults within 18–60. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures/tables).

Excluded for E8: participants fall partly outside the target adult age range (reported ages 16–21, including minors <18), violating the review’s 18–60 years restriction. Study otherwise meets the methodological inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI working memory), I6 (within-subject contrasts vs. 0-back active control), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster-thresholding and reported coordinates), I8 (whole-brain results reported with MNI coordinates), I9 (working memory = established executive function domain), and I10 (reports participant ages, healthy status screening, imaging modality, and task paradigm). No other exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study is an fMRI, task-based investigation of working memory (n-back) in healthy young and older adults and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses and within-participant contrasts between loads. Thus, it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9. However, the provided full-text does not include numerical participant ages or age ranges (it refers to participant characteristics in Table 1, which is not included in the provided content). Inclusion criterion I10 requires relevant information about participant age; because age information cannot be confirmed from the provided text, I10 is not met. Additionally, the review exclusion criterion E8 (studies including participants outside the 18–60 range) cannot be assessed due to missing age data. Given that ALL inclusion criteria must be met and I10 is not satisfied in the provided material, the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are directly violated based on the provided content.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study of inhibitory control (antisaccade) with whole-brain voxelwise group analyses and reported coordinates, it includes participants younger than 18 (adolescents 13–17) alongside adults and is not restricted to an 18–60-year-old healthy adult sample. This violates exclusion criterion E8 for the meta-analysis focused on healthy adults only. Additionally, the reported contrasts focus on reward vs neutral conditions within the antisaccade task and task epochs vs fixation baseline; the manuscript does not provide a within-participant contrast of the executive function (inhibition) task relative to an active non-inhibitory control condition required by inclusion criterion I6. Therefore, despite meeting I5, I7, I8, I9, and I10, the study must be excluded from this adult-focused meta-analysis.

This study meets multiple inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10): it is a task-based fMRI study of an executive function (working memory) n-back paradigm; includes within-participant contrasts (3-back vs 1-back); reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps (with coordinates and thresholds); task falls within executive function; and participant/sample, imaging modality, and task details are reported. However, it must be excluded under E8 because the sample includes participants older than the allowed age range (older group aged 60–71), i.e., includes participants outside 18–60. No other exclusion criteria are met. Inclusion criteria not met: none.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) in healthy adults (ages 20–40). It reports within-participant contrasts (distractor-plus vs control; correct vs error trials), uses group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses across the whole brain (SPM99), and reports activation peaks/coordinates in tables and figures. Participant/sample details, imaging modality, and task paradigm are fully described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; not between-group patient comparisons; active control present; empirical with healthy adults). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 19–31) using task-switching paradigms (response-switching and visual-switching) that probe cognitive flexibility/executive control. It reports within-participant, within-group voxelwise contrasts (switch vs stay) analyzed with random-effects, whole-brain statistical maps and thresholding, with peak coordinates provided in tables/figures. Participant characteristics, imaging modality (fMRI), and detailed task paradigms are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical, participants are within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an fMRI task study of cognitive control/executive function (temporal integration, working memory, strategy maintenance) in healthy adults (n=26, mean age 22.4). It reports within-subject contrasts between task conditions (W2 vs W12) and state/item decompositions, and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (cluster tables/coordinates, maps versus fixation and between-condition contrasts). Participant health status, age, imaging modality, and task details are reported. No exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because the sample includes participants outside the eligible age range (range 18–62 years), violating exclusion criterion E8. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI examining cognitive control/vigilance/working-memory updating in an oddball paradigm), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps reported for target-interval effects, with FWE correction and coordinates), I8 (whole-brain results reported and described in text/tables/figures), I9 (task falls within established executive domains: vigilance/working memory updating), and I10 (participant age range, healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 — the paper does not explicitly report a within-participant contrast of the executive task relative to an active control condition (e.g., target>standard); analyses focus on parametric modulation of target/novel responses by interval rather than an explicit task>active-control contrast. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) in healthy adults (n=16, ages 21–33). It includes within-subject contrasts (memory vs control; manipulable vs non-manipulable) and reports group-level, whole-brain, random-effects voxelwise analyses with coordinates and figures. An active control task was used (digit comparison), not rest/fixation. Participant health, age range, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigm are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, and participants are healthy and within 18–60). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory and visual search in healthy adults (ages 19–32). It reports within-participant contrasts including dual-task vs an active control (‘Visual search only’) and other task contrasts, uses group-level, whole-brain random-effects SPM analyses with voxelwise statistical maps and reports coordinates/tables, and provides detailed participant, imaging modality (1.5T fMRI) and task-paradigm information. The tasks fall within an executive function domain (working memory). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/rest-only, between-group-only, non-empirical, out-of-range or unhealthy samples) are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and none of the exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study used an N-back working-memory (executive) task with within-subject 2-back vs 0-back contrasts, reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise activations (coordinates/figures), and provides participant ages, healthy control status, imaging modality, and task details (meets I5–I10). However, the sample includes patient groups (NPSLE and RA) alongside healthy controls and is not restricted to healthy individuals, which violates exclusion criterion E8. Although within-group contrasts for healthy participants are reported, the inclusion of non-healthy participants means the study does not satisfy the meta-analysis requirement to be restricted to healthy adults. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Decision: EXCLUDED due to E8.

Exclusion IDs met: E3 (study reports ROI-based regional glucose metabolism analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps), E5 (no within-group whole-brain task activation contrast reported for healthy participants; analyses are correlational/ROI and between-group), and E8 (study includes patient sample and is not restricted to healthy individuals). Inclusion IDs met: I5 (PET study of executive function using Stroop task), I9 (task falls within executive function/inhibition domain), I10 (participant ages, healthy control status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion IDs not met: I6 (no reported within-participant contrast of task vs active control at the imaging-analysis level), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps provided), I8 (no whole-brain results reported via coordinates/figures for voxelwise maps). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded for this meta-analysis focused on whole-brain task activation maps in healthy adults.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of feature-based attentional control in healthy adults (mean age 24.3). The paradigm probes voluntary shifts of attention (cognitive control / cognitive flexibility) with within-subject contrasts comparing shift versus hold conditions. Analyses used a random-effects, whole-brain GLM with cluster-corrected voxelwise maps and reported Talairach coordinates and event-related timecourses. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task details are reported. Thus all required inclusion criteria are met (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, rest-only baselines, non-empirical design, or out-of-range/clinical participants). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study examining cognitive control/attentional control over threat-related distractors (executive function domain). It reports within-participant contrasts (threat-related vs neutral distractor trials; block × trial interactions) and analyses modulated by state anxiety. Group-level voxelwise/random-effects analyses were conducted with whole-brain corrections and ROI small-volume corrections; coordinates and figures are reported. Participants are healthy adults (age 18–38) and imaging modality and task paradigm are fully described. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is an empirical, task-based fMRI investigation of cognitive control in healthy adults (n=21, mean age 33) using the Preparing to Overcome Prepotency (POP) task. It reports within-participant task contrasts (high-control vs low-control trials) and trial-by-trial analyses, and presents group-level voxelwise/task-related activations and whole-brain cluster results (figures/tables and supplementary tables). Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary materials are referenced but not required for core eligibility. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of cognitive flexibility (task-switching) in healthy young adults, reporting within-subject contrasts (e.g., bivalent > univalent; switch > repeat) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (thresholded maps and tables/figures). Participant status (healthy, right-handed young adults), imaging modality (1.5T fMRI) and detailed task paradigm are described. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore, all inclusion criteria are met (I5–I10) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=14; ages 19–44) that explicitly investigates response inhibition, an established executive function domain. The study reports within-participant task contrasts (correct response inhibitions/lures versus target responses), and conducts group-level, whole-brain voxelwise one-sample t tests with cluster-level thresholding. Results are reported as stereotaxic coordinates (Table 1) and figures, and participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are clearly described. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only analyses, no connectivity/rest-only analyses, no between-group-only contrasts, participants are healthy and within 18–60 yrs, and this is primary empirical data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is an fMRI/NIRS investigation of spatial working memory with whole-brain, voxelwise analyses and reports coordinates; it includes healthy adult control within-group results and provides participant and task details. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI of executive function - working memory), I7 (group-level whole-brain maps), I8 (coordinates and figures reported), I9 (task is working memory, an executive function), I10 (participant, modality and task information reported). However, the study does not include an active control condition contrast; the task-related analyses use fixation/ITI or correct vs error trials and contrasts appear to be task vs baseline (fixation) or within-task performance contrasts rather than an executive task vs an active control task. The review exclusion criterion E6 (rest or fixation as the only baseline condition without an active control task) is therefore met. Inclusion criterion I6 (within-participant contrast of task relative to an active control) is not met. Because E6 is met and I6 is not satisfied, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI task study of visuospatial working memory (2-back) comparing users and controls. It reports a within-participant contrast (2-back minus match-to-center) and group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with coordinates and figures. Participants are aged 19–21 and screened for Axis I disorders (healthy sample), and modality, task paradigm, and participant details are reported. The control condition is an active match-to-center task (not fixation). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an event-related fMRI study of prosaccade vs antisaccade tasks (antisaccade involves inhibitory cognitive control). It reports within-subject contrasts (antisaccade vs prosaccade), group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps with cluster correction and coordinates, and provides participant ages and healthy-sample status, imaging modality, and detailed task paradigm. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study must be excluded because it violates the age restriction for the meta-analysis and lacks the required active-control within-subject contrast. Exclusion criteria met: E8 (sample includes participants outside the 18–60 age range — older group mean age 70.3) and E6 (analyses use an implicit/rest baseline rather than an active control condition for the executive-task contrasts). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I5 (task-based fMRI including an executive-domain task: working memory), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses conducted with SPM and random-effects), I8 (whole-brain results reported as tables/coordinates/figures), I9 (tasks include established executive-domain WM and vigilance/attention), and I10 (participant ages, healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigms are reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast of the executive task relative to an active control condition — contrasts are versus implicit baseline/rest). Because E8 (and E6) are violated, the study is ineligible for inclusion in this meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study of cognitive control/decision-making in healthy adults. It includes within-subject contrasts between task conditions (uncertain vs probable vs certain; probable wins vs probable losses), reports whole-brain voxelwise activation maps (figures and exploratory whole-brain analyses), and provides participant demographics and task details. The paradigm probes executive function/cognitive control (decision under uncertainty, response conflict, performance monitoring). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present.

This is an fMRI task study of working memory in healthy adults (meets I5, I9) that reports group-level voxelwise analyses within an independently derived load-dependent mask and presents whole-brain results/figures (meets I7 and I8). Participant demographics, healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported (meets I10). However, the within-subject contrasts are task vs session baseline (overall/rest baseline) rather than an active control condition. The study therefore does not meet I6 (requires a within-participant contrast against an active control) and violates exclusion criterion E6 (rest/fixation baseline only). Full text appears complete. Because I6 is not satisfied, the study must be excluded.

The study reports task-based fMRI (MSIT) probing executive/cognitive control (I5). It includes within-participant contrasts (incongruent > congruent) and reports behavioral RT/interference measures (I6). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are performed and results are reported with clusterwise thresholds, tables/figures and coordinates (I7,I8). The MSIT is an established executive function/inhibition/conflict task (I9). Participant information, confirmation of a healthy control sample, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are described (I10). Although the paper also includes an opiate-dependent group, it provides within-group healthy-control whole-brain activation maps and contrasts, so no exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI empirical study of verbal working memory (2-back), an established executive function domain. It uses a within-participant task contrast (2-back task blocks vs an active control letter-detection block) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps (one-sample t-tests, corrected cluster thresholds) with coordinates and figures. Participants are healthy college students (screened for neurologic/psychiatric conditions), imaging modality and task paradigm are clearly described. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Note: participant ages are reported as college students and matched between groups (healthy, born/raised >18 years for high-altitude group), which satisfies the requirement for age and healthy-sample reporting for this adult sample.

This is a task-based fMRI study of the Stroop (executive control/inhibition) in healthy adults (mean age 27.8). It reports within-subject contrasts (incongruent vs. congruent) and uses group-level, whole-brain analyses (PLS and SPM second-level results reported with clusters/coordinates). Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are all described. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, rest-only baseline, non-empirical, or out-of-range/unhealthy participants) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This fMRI study uses a Stroop inhibition task (an executive function paradigm) with within-participant contrasts (incongruent vs congruent) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps (analysed with XBAM) for healthy controls. The paper provides relevant participant information (control group age mean 33.3, confirmation of healthy status), imaging modality (1.5 T fMRI), and task paradigm details. Controls demonstrate significant within-group activations in canonical Stroop regions; the results are described in the text and reported as whole-brain findings (with supplementary figures/online material noted). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes a within-group map for healthy participants, uses an active control condition, empirical human neuroimaging data, and healthy participants are within 18–60 years). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Thus the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study investigates nonspatial selective vs divided attention and reports increased activity in lateral prefrontal and posterior parietal areas linked to attention and working memory. It uses a within-subject contrast comparing uncertainty (divided attention) versus certainty (selective attention) as an active control, includes whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM2, corrected thresholds) with reported coordinates and figures, and provides participant ages and healthy-sample confirmation. Therefore it meets criteria for task-based neuroimaging of executive-related processes (working memory/attention), within-participant active contrasts, whole-brain results, and required reporting.

This randomized, double-blind study used task-based fMRI in healthy adults (ages 40–60) to examine cognitive tasks that map onto executive function domains (spatial working memory and verbal memory). The imaging analyses include within-participant contrasts that serve as active-control contrasts (5-dot minus 3-dot spatial working memory; verbal old vs new), and group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) statistical maps are reported with stereotaxic coordinates (Table 3 and figures). Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigms are described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, includes within-group task contrasts, healthy adults within age range). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adult participants using the anti-saccade task, a canonical inhibitory-control (executive function) paradigm. The study reports within-subject contrasts (anti- vs pro-saccade and saccade vs fixation), uses task-based fMRI, and provides voxelwise activation results with statistical thresholding and cluster correction. Group-level summary results are presented (mean Talairach coordinates, figures of activation maps), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps (reported as coordinates/figures). The task falls within the inhibition domain of executive function. The Methods report participant sample size, healthy status, imaging modality (fMRI), and detailed task paradigm and timing. The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references and appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a PET study of a continuous performance (vigilance) task and includes healthy control participants, but it does not provide the required within-participant task vs active-control contrast nor whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation maps. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (analyses are ROI-based using 60 rectangular ROIs with no whole-brain voxelwise results reported) and E5 (the paper focuses on patient vs control comparisons and predictors of treatment response without presenting a within-group task activation contrast for healthy participants). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (PET study assessing an executive function task), I9 (task falls under vigilance), I10 (participant ages, healthy-control status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast of task relative to an active control condition), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map). Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 23–47) directly probes initiation and inhibition — executive function domains (initiation, inhibition). It includes within-subject contrasts between task conditions (e.g., ballistic vs smooth for initiation; stepwise vs ballistic or smooth for inhibition), where smooth movement served as an active control. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (cluster-thresholded maps and stereotactic coordinates), and results are described in the text and figures/tables. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (3T fMRI) and task paradigm are provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not patient-only contrasts, and participants are within 18–60 and healthy). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for this review.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults using a visuospatial n-back working memory task (an executive function). The paper reports within-subject task contrasts (memory-load-dependent/linear n-back contrasts using 0-,1-,2-,3-back blocks), group-level random-effects whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM99, p_corrected<0.05) with coordinates and figures, and provides participant demographics and health status. The task falls within the working memory domain. Full methods, results, and discussion are presented, so the full text appears complete. Thus all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of cognitive control/executive function (working memory load and distractor interference). It reports within-participant contrasts (incongruent vs congruent; load × congruency interactions) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps with thresholds and cluster results. Tasks fall within executive domains (working memory, inhibition/response control). Participant demographics (healthy adults aged 18–35), imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are clearly reported. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not truncated). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, resting-state baseline, non-empirical, or out-of-range/clinical samples) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and should be included.

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory updating (an executive function) in healthy adults (n=12, ages 19–34). The paper reports within-subject contrasts (update > cued maintenance; memory blocks > category discrimination control), and performs group-level, voxelwise whole-brain GLM analyses with voxelwise thresholds and cluster correction; results and coordinates are described and referenced (including supplementary tables). Participant health status, ages, imaging modality (fMRI), and detailed task paradigm are reported. Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not a between-group patient study, uses active control conditions, is empirical with original human neuroimaging data, and participants are within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of visual working memory (an executive function) in healthy adults (ages 22–36). It includes within-subject contrasts (WM vs fixation-control and correct vs incorrect trials), reports group-level whole-brain voxel-wise maps (fixed-effects group Z maps) supplemented by random-effects ROI analyses, and presents results in figures/tables. Imaging modality, participant health status/ages, and task paradigm are all reported. The fixation-control condition included active button-press responses (an active control), so it does not meet the exclusion for using only rest/fixation as baseline. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of working memory/attentional control (three-back task with lure vs non-lure trials), sampling healthy adults (age 18–37). Analyses include within-participant contrasts between task conditions (lure vs non-lure; event-related trial-type effects) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported cluster coordinates (Table 1 and figures). Task is an established executive-function paradigm (working memory/interference control). Participant demographics, health screening, imaging modality, and task details are reported. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria relevant to the meta-analysis (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10).

This is an empirical fMRI study of executive function (task-switching cognitive control) in healthy adults (N=19). It includes within-subject contrasts (shift vs repeat; high vs low response and stimulus conflict), conducted as group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM analyses with reported thresholds and coordinates (whole-brain results and ROI follow-ups; supplemental data referenced). Participant age/health status, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and detailed task paradigm and methods are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group only, not non-empirical, participants are healthy adults within 18–60). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an event-related fMRI study of executive function (proactive interference/inhibition within a modified WCST) in healthy adults. It meets inclusion criteria: (I5) imaging modality fMRI and task-based executive control (inhibition/cognitive flexibility); (I6) within-subject contrast of interest (control vs. release trials; control minus release) isolating inhibition; (I7) group-level whole-brain, voxelwise analyses using SPM2 with reported thresholding and FDR correction and coordinate tables/figures; (I8) whole-brain results are reported as figures and coordinate tables and described in text; (I9) task falls within cognitive flexibility/inhibition executive domains; (I10) participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported (N=78, age 20–28, healthy). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, rest-only baseline, non-empirical paper, or out-of-range/clinical sample). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion and references (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that includes a canonical executive-function task (2-back working memory) and reports within-subject task contrasts. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain analyses and group fMRI maps (figures and text) for the 2-back task, and reports participant ages (mean 27, range 22–52), healthy sample status, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigm details. The 2-back design uses alternating task and active-control epochs (including a TAP response instruction during control epochs), supporting a within-participant contrast against an active control condition. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (age 18–37) that examines executive function domains including working memory and associative memory. The paper reports within-participant task contrasts with active control conditions (STERN: novel vs practiced/RT control; PMT: associative learning vs simple classification). Group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) statistical maps were generated and reported (thresholded whole-brain maps, ROIs derived from these contrasts; results presented in figures/tables), and coordinates/ROIs are described. Participant demographics, healthy-sample screening, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigms are reported. No exclusion criteria are met: the study is not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, includes within-group task activation contrasts, and participants are healthy adults within 18–60. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis.

While this is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) with group-level whole-brain maps and within-subject contrasts across difficulty levels, the full text as provided does not report ages for the healthy volunteer sample. The inclusion criteria require relevant information about participant age in addition to healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task paradigm. Age information for the nine healthy participants is absent in the provided text, so inclusion criterion I10 is not satisfied. All other inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9) are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This study reports original task-based fMRI data in healthy young adults (median age 22, range 18–25) using an n-back working memory task (executive function). The authors performed within-subject contrasts (two-back vs active ‘x-target’ baseline) and second-level random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2) with reported cluster coordinates and thresholds. Task paradigm, participant health status, age range, and imaging modality are clearly described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task activations, uses an active baseline, empirical fMRI data, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and none of the exclusion criteria.

This study does not meet the review population and task-domain requirements. Exclusion criteria met: E8 — the sample includes older adults with MCI and AD (not restricted to healthy adults aged 18–60). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (group-level, whole-brain task-evoked maps and voxelwise analyses are reported using GLM and Talairach transformations), I8 (whole-brain results are described and illustrated in figures/tables), I10 (participant age/education, healthy control status for the control group, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (the fMRI task assesses semantic memory/naming, not an executive function/cognitive control task), I6 (no within-participant contrast of an executive function task vs an active control condition is provided), I9 (task does not fall within established executive function domains such as working memory, inhibition, or cognitive flexibility). Because E8 is violated (participants are not a healthy adult sample within 18–60 only), the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis despite some whole-brain reporting.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adult bilinguals (mean age 25.4) that explicitly investigates language control — a form of cognitive control involving inhibition/switching. It includes within-subject contrasts comparing selection contexts (e.g., LSc vs SNc, LSc vs TSc, L2 vs L1) against active naming/control conditions. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain random-effects SPM2 results reported in figures and coordinate tables. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (fMRI, 1.5T), and detailed task paradigms are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5–I10 and does not violate any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or resting-baseline-only design; participants are healthy and age within 18–60).

This is an fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=20, ages 19–26) using a Stroop-like task assessing attentional control/inhibition (an executive function). It reports within-participant contrasts (incongruent vs. congruent targets) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (thresholded at p<.05 FDR; coordinates and tables provided). Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, includes within-group task contrasts, uses active task baselines, empirical human neuroimaging data, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adult volunteers (mean age 32) that directly investigates task switching (cognitive flexibility), an executive function. It reports within-subject contrasts (switching vs non-switching; semantic-category vs overlearned sequences) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM with corrected thresholds and tabulated stereotactic coordinates and figures. Participant characteristics, imaging modality, and task paradigms are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/rest-only, between-group-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range/unhealthy sample) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=10, mean age 29±10) that directly contrasts executive-function-related conditions against active control conditions. The spatial attention and memory paradigm (SAMP) involves working memory/attentional demands (an established executive domain). The paper reports within-participant (task vs control) contrasts and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM with voxelwise and cluster-level thresholds; peak coordinates and activation tables are provided. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), and detailed task paradigms are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical, participants are healthy and within 18–60). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the report is complete for screening purposes.

Full text not accessible from provided content (redirect notice). Based on title/metadata, this is an fMRI study of verbal working memory (supporting I5 and I9). However, the full article (methods/results) is not available here, so I cannot confirm key required details: (I6) that a within-participant contrast versus an active control was performed, (I7) that group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps are reported (or coordinates/figures clearly described per I8), and (I10) participant age range and confirmation of healthy adults. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) can be confirmed as met from the available information. Therefore the study is excluded due to incomplete/full-text inability to verify inclusion criteria.

This is a prospective task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 18–35) that includes executive-function paradigms (working memory STERN; also attention), reports within-participant contrasts versus active control conditions (e.g., NT vs CT for working memory; AL vs SC and RE vs SC for associative memory), and conducts group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (group contrast maps, voxel-by-voxel SPM2 analyses with FWE correction; ROIs derived from whole-brain contrasts with MNI coordinates). Participant health status, age range, imaging modality, and task paradigms are clearly reported. None of the exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, includes within-group task activations, includes active control contrasts, empirical fMRI data in healthy adults).

This is an fMRI study of an executive (working memory) task (spatial n-back) with reward manipulations in healthy adults (mean age 21.7). It includes within-subject contrasts (3-back vs 1-back; reward vs no-reward and interactions), uses group-level random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses with reported thresholds and tables of coordinates, and provides participant, task, and imaging details. An active control (0-back) was used. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 29–41) using a task that engages executive processes (guessing/gambling with working-memory and decision-making demands). It includes a within-subject contrast of an executive task (guessing) versus an active control (reporting) with matched perceptual/motor demands. Analyses are whole-brain voxelwise SPM group-level maps with reported activation foci/coordinates and figures/tables. Sufficient participant, imaging modality, and paradigm details are reported. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical fMRI study using the N-back working memory task (executive function). It reports within-participant 2-back > 0-back contrasts, processed with SPM5 and second-level random-effects voxelwise analyses. Whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (reporting results within a priori DLPFC via small-volume correction) and figures/coordinates are provided for significant loci. Participants are healthy adult volunteers (sample sizes and screening described; imaging sample demographics and age were reported/controlled and referenced in Supplementary Table 5), imaging modality (BOLD fMRI) and task paradigm (N-back working memory) are clearly described. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function fMRI with within-subject active-control contrast and group-level voxelwise maps. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete.

Full text is incomplete/unavailable (content only shows a redirect/placeholder). Cannot verify core methods or results against inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met / not verifiable: I5 (fMRI/PET task assessing executive function), I6 (within-participant contrast vs active control), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map), I8 (clear reporting of whole-brain results), I9 (task falls within executive function domains), I10 (participant age/healthy status/imaging modality/task reported). Exclusion criteria applied: none can be confidently applied from the provided content (e.g., E3–E8 cannot be assessed without full methods/results). Because the full text is incomplete, this study must be excluded from the meta-analysis until the complete article is obtained and re-screened.

This is an original task-based fMRI study of executive function (branching integrating working memory and attentional allocation). It reports within-participant contrasts (branching vs control, delay, dual-task) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates and statistical thresholds (tables/figures). Participants were healthy right-handed adults aged 20–28. Imaging modality (fMRI), task paradigms (working memory, dual-task, planning/branching), and participant/sample details are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, includes within-group contrasts, uses active control condition, empirical data, participants within 18–60 and healthy).

Full text appears to describe a resting-state fMRI study of mild cognitive impairment and mild Alzheimer’s disease rather than a task-based executive function study in healthy adults. Exclusion IDs met: E4 (resting-state/connectivity analyses without a whole-brain task activation map) and E8 (not restricted to healthy individuals; includes patient groups). Inclusion IDs met: none []. Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (not a task-based executive function fMRI/PET study), I6 (no within-participant task vs active control contrast reported), I7 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation map), I9 (tasks are not within executive function domains), I10 (insufficient/irrelevant reporting for healthy adult task paradigm). Full text provided appears incomplete (only metadata/redirect page), so fulltext_incomplete=true.

This is an fMRI study of working memory (n-back) with whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses and within-participant task contrasts (e.g., 2-back vs 0-back). It meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. However, the sample includes both patients with schizophrenia and healthy comparison subjects (i.e., the study is not restricted to healthy adults), which violates exclusion criterion E8 (studies not restricted to healthy individuals). Therefore the study must be excluded from a meta-analysis restricted to healthy adult executive-function activations. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: none. Exclusion criteria met: E8.

This is an fMRI study of a NoGo (inhibition) task, which is an established executive function domain. The paper reports within-participant contrasts (NoGo vs Go) and presents group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses for healthy control subjects (contrast images, β images, and tables/figures with coordinates). Participant information (healthy control group described, demographics referenced in Table 1), imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are reported. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing verification of criteria. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without within-group healthy contrasts, resting-only baseline, non-empirical, or out-of-range participants) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI study of healthy adults using working memory tasks (delayed recognition) with event-related, whole-brain group analyses; participant ages and health status are reported. However, the paper does not present a within-participant contrast of an executive task versus an active control task condition. The reported analyses focus on task-period activity (cue, delay, probe) using main-effect-of-task maps (conjunctions) and comparisons to baseline, rather than an active control task. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 is not met, and exclusion criterion E6 applies (use of rest/fixation or baseline-only contrasts without an active control). Full text appears complete.

Exclusion: The study does not investigate an established executive function task domain (it examines auditory spatial attention reorienting in a passive listening paradigm) and does not present a within-participant contrast of an executive task relative to an active control. Additionally, the primary task contrasts are reported versus a REST (silent) baseline (i.e., rest/fixation), fitting exclusion E6. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps are reported), I8 (whole-brain results and coordinates are reported in tables/figures), and I10 (participant age, healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not an fMRI/PET study of executive function/cognitive control task), I6 (no within-participant contrast against an active control condition), and I9 (task does not fall within established executive function domains such as working memory, inhibition, or cognitive flexibility). Full text appears complete for screening.

This study is excluded because it reports primarily EEG-derived connectivity analyses (PDC and graph-theoretic measures) and does not provide a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map from fMRI or PET. Exclusion criteria met: E4 (reports only connectivity analyses without an accompanying whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (within-participant contrast: congruent vs. incongruent Stroop conditions), I9 (task is Stroop — an executive/inhibition paradigm), I10 (reports participant age, healthy status, imaging modalities, and task details). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not a task-activation fMRI/PET study reporting task-evoked activations), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map presented), I8 (no whole-brain activation coordinates/voxelwise maps described). Full text appears complete for screening. Therefore the paper does not satisfy required whole-brain fMRI/PET activation evidence and must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=14, age 26–42) using a covert orienting task to probe inhibition of return (IOR). The study reports within-subject contrasts (long SOA vs short SOA) to isolate IOR-related effects, and uses group-level, whole-brain random-effects SPM analyses with corrected thresholds and reports peak coordinates and figures. Participant demographics, health-status screening, imaging modality (fMRI), and detailed task paradigm are all reported. IOR indexes an inhibitory attentional process and maps onto the ‘inhibition’ domain within executive function constructs. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, active task control, healthy adults within 18–60). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so is complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of an executive-function task (colour Stroop; inhibition) in healthy adults (N=28, mean age 20.2). The paper reports within-participant contrasts (parametric linear trend across blocks varying proportion of incongruent trials and supplementary contrasts of each incongruity level vs 0% baseline), and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates and figures (P<0.001 uncorrected). Participant details, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported. The 0% incongruent blocks provide an active baseline/control condition. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not resting-state-only, participants are healthy and adult). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an fMRI study with whole-brain group-level activation maps in healthy adults (meets I7, I8, I10). However, the task is autobiographical emotion induction (irritability/happiness) rather than a canonical executive-function/cognitive-control task (e.g., working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility). Therefore it does not satisfy I5 (task assessing executive function/cognitive control) nor I9 (task within established executive function domains). Although within-subject contrasts are reported, they are contrasts of emotional states rather than an executive task contrast, so I6 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (N=16, ages 19–35) directly investigating cognitive control/executive function (contextual and episodic control, task switching/conflict). The paper reports within-participant, group-level voxelwise whole-brain contrasts and factorial analyses (SPM2; voxelwise and cluster thresholds; FDR correction) and presents coordinates/figures of activations. Detailed methods, participant health/age, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigms are reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of working memory (delayed item recognition for letters) in healthy adults (n=40, mean age 25.1) that reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (second-level GLM and MLM) and presents coordinates/figures of activation. The paper includes within-participant contrasts across task conditions (set-size/load comparisons and delay-period effects) that serve as active cognitive-control contrasts (low vs. intermediate vs. high WM load). Participant demographics, health screening, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria are met: the study is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task contrasts, and participants are healthy adults within the 18–60 range. The full article (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an fMRI empirical study of working memory (n-back phonological and spatial tasks) in healthy adults. It reports within-subject contrasts between executive task conditions (PWM>SWM and SWM>PWM) and task>baseline contrasts, uses group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2) with coordinates and thresholding described, and provides participant age, health status, imaging modality, and task details. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not rest-only baseline without active contrasts, not non-empirical, participants are healthy adults within 18–60). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10.

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory control/integration (an executive function domain). It reports within-subject contrasts among task conditions (IN vs SG, MO, RO) and voxelwise group-level random-effects whole-brain analyses with coordinates and brain maps. Participant information (healthy adults, ages reported), imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are described in detail. The study therefore meets inclusion criteria I5–I10. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group only, not non-empirical, and participants are healthy adults within 18–60). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

Although this study reports group-level whole-brain fMRI analyses and provides full participant and task details, it does not assess canonical executive function domains required by the review. The main tasks are object categorization and recognition (perceptual/memory tasks), and the mental-rotation localizer probes visuo-spatial transformation rather than an established executive domain (e.g., working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility). The report does not present a within-participant contrast of an executive function task vs an active control that would meet I6/I9. Therefore it fails I5, I6, and I9 despite meeting I7, I8, and I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) apply. Full text appears complete.

While the study is an fMRI study of inhibition (modified RPS) in healthy adults and reports whole-brain group-level voxelwise results, it does not include a within-participant contrast of an executive task relative to an active control condition. The fMRI analyses reported are task versus rest within groups and a between-group (lose vs win) comparison; subjects were assigned to win or lose groups rather than performing both conditions within-subject. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (within-participant contrast vs an active control) is not met. Exclusion criterion E6 applies because the within-subject baseline contrasts use rest/fixation without an active control task. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criterion not met: I6. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly investigates cognitive control/conflict monitoring (ACC–PFC) during semantic retrieval (the TOT state). It contains within-participant contrasts comparing TOT versus Know and Don’t Know conditions (active task conditions), reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with corrected statistics (SPM, p<0.05 cluster-corrected), and provides participant demographics (14 healthy adults, ages 19–27), imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), and task paradigm details. Thus it meets I5 (fMRI study of cognitive control), I6 (within-subject contrasts against active conditions), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described in text/tables/figures), I9 (examines cognitive control/monitoring processes within executive function domain), and I10 (reports participant age, healthy status, modality, and paradigm). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain) in healthy adults (8 participants, ages 20–25). The paper reports within-participant contrasts of executive tasks versus matched active control conditions (REP/REP CONT, MAT/MAT CONT, REP/MAT). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM) are reported, with thresholding corrected for multiple comparisons and cluster extent criteria; results are presented as statistical maps and described in the text/tables. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigms are all reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) are satisfied. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of a sustained attention (CPT) task in healthy adults (ages 18–28) that reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps (SPM) comparing task blocks to baseline. CPT falls within the review’s executive-function domain (vigilance). Methods report a within-subject contrast of active CPT versus a baseline of meaningless images (visual control), which serves as an active control condition rather than simple fixation. Relevant participant information (age, health status), imaging modality (fMRI), and task details are provided. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a within-subject task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (N=23, mean age 21.3) probing selective/object-based attention and top-down cognitive control. It reports within-participant contrasts (attend vs ignore/observe) using active control conditions, and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (conjunctions and state contrasts) with thresholding described. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported. The selective attention task targets cognitive control/top-down biasing processes and thus falls within executive/cognitive-control domains relevant to the review. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task contrasts, uses active control conditions, healthy adult sample). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of inhibitory control (GO/NOGO), an executive function, with healthy adult participants (N=15, age 23–40). It reports within-subject contrasts of task events (successful Stops/NOGO) relative to baseline/Go conditions and conducts group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (Talairach normalization, voxelwise thresholds, cluster correction). Results are presented as whole-brain activation maps and described in text/tables/figures. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), and task paradigm are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so full text is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This paper reports an fMRI study in healthy adults using an n-back working-memory paradigm (an executive function task) with within-subject contrasts (n-back levels vs 0-back control and parametric complexity contrasts). Group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) random-effects analyses are reported and thresholded; coordinates and cluster tables are provided. Participant characteristics (healthy right-handed volunteers, sample size, matching to controls) and imaging modality (1.5T fMRI) and task details are described. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Inclusion criteria applied: I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10. Exclusion criteria applied: [].

This fMRI study includes a working-memory (n-back) manipulation (executive function domain) with within-subject contrasts (high > low WM load) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (random-effects SPM results with voxel coordinates and thresholding). Participants are healthy adults (16 males, age 22–30). Imaging modality, task paradigm, and participant details are reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adult participants (Experiment 1: n=12, mean age 25±3.3; Experiment 2: n=12, mean age 22±4.1) investigating top-down attentional control (zooming in/out), which the authors frame as executive/cognitive control processes. The paper reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., zooming in/out vs high-level baseline [HLB]; zooming out > zooming in; zooming in > zooming out) and performs group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2; cluster- and voxel-level thresholds reported) with coordinates/tables. Task paradigm and imaging modality (fMRI) are fully described. Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, resting-only baseline, non-empirical paper, or out-of-range/clinical sample). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study investigates nonspatial attention shifting (feature-based set-shifting) in healthy adults using within-subject contrasts (shifting attention vs sustained attention) and reports voxelwise group results with Talairach coordinates. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of cognitive control), I6 (within-participant contrast of executive-like task vs active control), I8 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates/figures), I9 (task maps to cognitive flexibility/set-shifting), I10 (participants’ ages, healthy status, imaging modality, and paradigm reported). However, the study does NOT meet I7: although voxelwise group analyses were performed, imaging coverage was limited to posterior brain and cerebellum (coronal slices covering occipital/parietal/part temporal and cerebellum) and did not provide whole-brain coverage (frontal regions were not imaged), so there is no qualifying whole-brain group-level activation map. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered. Therefore exclude because I7 is not satisfied.

Excluded because the study includes participants outside the target population for the meta-analysis: it includes a patient group (Turner syndrome) rather than being restricted to healthy adults, and includes participants younger than 18 (age range for Turner group includes 14-year-old), thus violating exclusion criterion E8. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function — working memory tasks), I6 (within-participant contrasts across task conditions/domains and distracter vs no-distracter), I9 (tasks fall within executive function domain — working memory), I10 (participant ages, health status of control group, imaging modality and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no clear report of a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical map in the main text; results are primarily ROI-based with group-average activation maps reported in supplementary figures but no clearly described voxelwise group-level statistical maps for inclusion). Because E8 is met, the study must be excluded from a meta-analysis restricted to healthy adults aged 18–60.

This fMRI study investigates voluntary suppression of thermally induced pain, reporting whole-brain group voxelwise activations and healthy adult sample details. However, the suppression condition is contrasted against rest (a passive baseline) rather than an active control task; there is no within-participant contrast of the executive/suppression task relative to an active control. Therefore it fails exclusion criterion E6 (rest/fixation as only baseline). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task engages cognitive control/inhibition), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I8 (results reported with figures/tables/coodinates), I9 (task taps an executive domain: inhibition), I10 (participant age/health, imaging modality, paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast vs an active control). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Excluded because the study reports only region-of-interest analyses (no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation maps are presented in this paper) and primarily uses task vs. fixation (rest) contrasts rather than an active control condition; additionally, the sample includes clinical participants (schizophrenia) and is not restricted to healthy adults. (a) Exclusion IDs met: E3 (ROI-only, no whole-brain results), E6 (rest/fixation used as the primary baseline for key contrasts), E8 (sample not restricted to healthy individuals). (b) Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task-based fMRI including working memory), I9 (task within executive function domain — working memory), I10 (reported participant demographics, healthy sample status for control group, imaging modality, and task paradigm). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast against an active control condition for the executive-task contrasts), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map presented in this full text). Thus the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and is excluded.

This fMRI study examines planning, monitoring, and rule-related cognition during driving — processes that map onto executive functions (planning, rule retrieval/maintenance). It uses within-subject contrasts (e.g., Action planning > Coasting; Monitoring traffic > Coasting; Traffic rules > Coasting) against an active baseline (coasting). Analyses were conducted with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise SPM models and peak coordinates/tables are reported. Participant demographic and health information, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are reported (20 healthy right-handed licensed taxi drivers, ages 27–59). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not connectivity/rest-only; not between-group-only; participants are healthy and within 18–60). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function activations.

Exclusion E3 met: the fMRI results are presented as individual subject activation images and ROI-based summary statistics (McNemar test across regions of interest) rather than a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical map or reported coordinates. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing executive function — auditory digital working memory), I6 (within-participant contrast of working memory vs an active non-working-memory control), I9 (task is working memory, an established executive domain), I10 (participant age, healthy sample status, imaging modality and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no clear group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map reported), and therefore I8 (acceptable reporting of whole-brain results via coordinates/figures) is not satisfied at the group/voxelwise level. Full text appears complete for decision-making. Given the lack of requisite whole-brain group-level voxelwise results, this study should be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (mean age reported) that investigates mental calculation tasks engaging working memory and manipulation (executive function). It reports within-subject contrasts of calculation versus active control conditions (result-matching, letter pseudo-calculation, substitution tasks). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed using SPM and results are reported in figures/tables. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and detailed task paradigms are described. Although the final analyzed sample is small (n=5) and a fixed-effects group model was used, these aspects do not violate the stated inclusion/exclusion criteria. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical PET study that assesses executive function (counting Stroop) in healthy adult volunteers. It includes within-subject contrasts of incongruent vs. neutral (active control) Stroop conditions, reported at the group level using voxelwise whole-brain SPM analyses (results presented in tables/figures). Participant ages and healthy status, imaging modality (H2(15)O PET), and task paradigm are clearly described. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. All inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are met.

Excluded because analyses were performed exclusively using region-of-interest (ROI) approaches with no group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map reported, thereby violating exclusion criterion E3. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing executive function — working memory), I6 (within-participant contrasts of task conditions), I9 (task falls within executive function domain: working memory), and I10 (participant ages reported, healthy sample, imaging modality and task paradigm described). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results provided). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Excluded because the study does not evaluate an executive function/cognitive-control task contrast required by the review. Although it is an fMRI, task-based, group-level whole-brain study (I7) with clearly reported results (I8) and reports participant/sample/task details (I10), the primary reported analyses focus on a monetary incentive delay reward task (not an executive function task) and the manuscript does not present a within-participant contrast of an executive function task versus an active control (I5, I6, I9 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study using a 2-back working memory task (an executive function domain). It reports within-participant contrasts among task conditions (Word, Cross, Within), including direct comparisons (e.g., Cross vs Within) and percent signal changes across conditions. Group-level random-effects whole-brain analyses were performed with FDR correction and reported activations with coordinates and figures. Participants are healthy adults (ages 20–28), imaging modality and task paradigm are clearly described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, active task contrasts beyond rest are reported, healthy adult sample within range). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This fMRI study uses a task that elicits cognitive interference (semantic–prosodic conflict) analogous to Stroop-like executive control tasks, and reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses contrasting incongruent (CONF) vs congruent (NOCONF) conditions. Participants are healthy adults (ages 24–38). Imaging modality (fMRI), task paradigm, behavioral results, and whole-brain statistical results are reported. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based executive function activations and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This article reports task-based fMRI of working memory (an executive function) with healthy control participants and patients. It includes within-participant contrasts of working memory tasks versus active control tasks (letter-case and form-judgment control conditions). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses are reported (cluster- and FWE-corrected results, with coordinates/tables and figures). Participant demographics and healthy sample matching are described; imaging modality (fMRI) and task paradigms are fully detailed. Although the sample includes patients, the paper provides within-group healthy control activation maps suitable for inclusion in a meta-analysis of executive function in healthy adults. Full text content (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present, so fulltext_incomplete is false. No exclusion criteria are met.

Although this is an fMRI study of a stop-signal (inhibition) task in healthy adults and reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., STOP vs GO, STOP-success vs STOP-fail) with participant ages and task details (meets I5, I6, I9, I10), the analyses are ROI-focused and the report does not provide a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map. The authors explicitly restricted analyses to anatomically defined ROIs and did not perform or report whole-brain group-level voxelwise results. Therefore this study violates exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) and fails inclusion criterion I7 (no group-level whole-brain map). Full text appears complete. Exclusion based on E3; included criteria met: I5, I6, I9, I10; inclusion criterion not met: I7.

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory and selective attention (executive domains) in healthy adult participants. It includes within-participant contrasts of executive tasks vs an active control (STERN: NT vs CT) and attention conditions (TO vs DO), and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (group maps, z-thresholds, cluster correction). Participant health status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigms are described; demographic matching and exclusion criteria are reported (see Table 1). The paper therefore meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not violate exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, includes within-group task activation maps, and uses active control contrasts). Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of executive control/dual-task processing in healthy adults (ages 19–32). It reports within-subject task contrasts (DM>SM, SM>SP) and pre/post training comparisons (Time × Group, Time × Group × Condition). The manuscript includes group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster-thresholded Z-stat maps) and tables/figures describing whole-head results as well as coordinate tables, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Participant demographics, health screening, imaging modality (3T fMRI) and detailed task paradigms are reported. Although hypothesis-driven ROI analyses are used, whole-brain results are also provided (including DLPFC increases and Time × Group whole-head maps), so the study is not ROI-only. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of executive control (color–word Stroop) in healthy adults (age 24–40). It reports within-subject contrasts (incongruent vs neutral; one-word vs four-word blocks) and group-level mixed-effects whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FLAME) with peak coordinates in tables and ROI follow-ups. Participant characteristics, imaging modality, and task paradigm are fully described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group only, not non-empirical, participants are healthy and within 18–60). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables) is present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This study is an fMRI task-based investigation with whole-brain group analyses in healthy adults (12 males, age 18–30). However, the paradigm primarily investigates imitation/perception–action matching and social-cognitive processes rather than a canonical executive function task. Although the authors discuss working memory and error-detection, the task does not clearly fall within established executive-function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation) as required by I9. Therefore it fails I5 (assessment of executive function/cognitive control) and I9 (task within established executive domains). Consequently I6 is not met because the within-participant contrasts are not contrasts of an identified executive function task vs an active control. The paper does meet I7, I8, and I10 (whole-brain group analyses, coordinates/tables reported, and participant/sample/imaging details provided). No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) in healthy adults (ages 18–28). It reports within-subject contrasts between binding conditions and an active single-item non-binding baseline, conducts group-level, whole-brain (second-level voxelwise) analyses (with FDR correction), and presents whole-brain results in figures/tables. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are clearly reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because it includes participants outside the eligible age range (subjects aged 18–80), thereby meeting exclusion criterion E8.
